transcript: This new play on Broadway, Call Me Izzy, did not really live up to its leading actress for me. Starring Jean Smart and marking the beginning of the 2025-2026 Broadway season, this solo show features women in Louisiana directly telling us the story of her abusive marriage. She pretty much has two lives — one with her husband in the trailer that they live in together, the other being a completely secret and internal place that holds all of her passions for writing and her dreams of something bigger. The character is pretty non specific, which some would argue universalizes her story, but to me, it leaned too far into archetype to keep me curious about her, though Jean Smart gave a great performance. There are plenty of questions this play could have investigated about her, like why she stays in this toxic relationship, or what factors led her to being with him in the first place, but it doesn't really go beyond the surface. It's more of a plot-driven, episodic narration than anything else and I ultimately found it a little slow and predictable, with writing that was kinda lackluster for a play about a woman who's supposedly a gifted poet. Call Me Izzy has some heavy material, so I’d use your discretion accordingly, but it also has humorous moments, and Jean Smart tactfully keeps this character grounded and avoids melodrama. She is the draw here — if you wanna see her specifically, then I'd say it's worth going. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
